verifications.claim: There was a DHS government shutdown in March 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: DHS shutdown ongoing in March 2026 (e.g., R2: 'shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) continues well into its sixth week'; R3: 'The shutdown of Homeland Security will reach 44 days on Sunday'; R6: testimony on March 25, 2026)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm DHS shutdown active throughout March 2026, with events dated in March.

verifications.claim: Roughly 60,000 TSA employees were required to work without pay during the March 2026 DHS government shutdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'About 95% of TSA's 60,000 employees are considered essential workers'; R2: 'more than 60,000 TSA employees... are not being paid'; R3: 'Roughly 60,000 TSA staff are going without pay'; R8: 'Roughly 60,000 TSA staff are going without pay'
verifications.reasoning: Exact number and context of essential workers required without pay directly match across sources.

verifications.claim: Hundreds of TSA employees quit during the March 2026 DHS government shutdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'hundreds of TSA agents have quit during the partial shutdown'; R2: 'nearly 500 transportation security officers have left their positions'; R3: 'nearly 500... have quit during the shutdown'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state hundreds (or nearly 500) TSA employees quit during the shutdown.

verifications.claim: Thousands of daily call-outs occurred among TSA employees during the March 2026 DHS government shutdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'thousands more have begun to call out sick at record rates'; R3: 'more than 3,450 callouts' (nationwide on Thursday); R6: 'daily call out rates... 11% nationwide'
verifications.reasoning: Sources report thousands of callouts, e.g., 3,450 in one day, during the shutdown.

verifications.claim: On March 27, 2026, President Trump signed an order to pay TSA employees using alternative funds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'President Donald Trump on Friday signed... executive action' (March 2026 article); R7: 'March 27, 2026'; R2/R4/R8: order to use alternative funds with 'reasonable and logical nexus'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm signing on March 27 (Friday) using alternative funds.

verifications.claim: Nearly 500 transportation security officers quit in March 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'nearly 500 transportation security officers have left'; R3: 'nearly 500... transportation security officers have quit'; R5: 'more than 500 officers to leave TSA'
verifications.reasoning: Precise figure 'nearly 500 TSOs' quit during March shutdown directly stated.

verifications.claim: Call-out rates reached 11% nationwide in March 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'more than 11.8%... nationwide'; R6: '11% nationwide'; R8: 'call-out rates have increased to 11% nationwide'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly report 11% or 11.8% nationwide call-out rates in March.

verifications.claim: Long wait times exceeding three hours occurred at some airports in March 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'security wait times... three or more hours'; R6: 'wait times to over four and half hours'; R7: 'wait times reaching up to three hours'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm wait times over three hours at airports during March.

verifications.claim: TSA workers missed three paychecks before the order to pay them was signed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R8: 'TSA employees missed their third paycheck of the partial government shutdown on Friday'
verifications.reasoning: R8 directly states third paycheck missed on Friday (March 27, order signing day).

verifications.claim: The Acting TSA Administrator reported that workers faced financial ruin, including selling plasma and sleeping in cars to stay on the job.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'sleeping in their cars... selling their blood and plasma'; R9: 'acting TSA leader Nguyen McNeill... "Some are sleeping in their cars, selling their blood and plasma"'
verifications.reasoning: Acting TSA leader's testimony quotes exact hardships.

verifications.claim: President Trump's order redirects funds with a "reasonable and logical nexus" to TSA operations to pay employees.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '"use funds that have a reasonable and logical nexus to TSA operations"'; identical phrasing in R3, R4, R5, R8
verifications.reasoning: Exact quote from the order text in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: ICE agents were deployed to airports to assist with staffing shortages.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Trump sent ICE officers to some U.S. airports... to alleviate hours-long security wait times'; R4: 'Trump ordered ICE agents be deployed at 14 major airports to assist TSA agents'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm ICE deployment to airports for TSA staffing help.

verifications.claim: TSA employees are slated to be paid under the executive order.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'TSA workers “should begin seeing paychecks as early as Monday”'; R4: 'TSA workers could start seeing their paychecks as soon as Monday'; R8: 'TSA staff would begin receiving paychecks “as early as” March 30'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state TSA employees to receive pay under the order soon after signing.
